observations: Photos 0 and 1 show the same scene from two angles: a shipping container on a truck, open at the back, packed on three shelves with used car engines.
A man in a red shirt and cap is marking or inspecting one engine with a pen.
The engines are mostly long blocks with flywheels or flexplates exposed and black timing covers, several look like V6 engines; at least a few dozen units are visible.
Some engines carry chalk or marker writing, but no engine code, brand plate or casting number can be read in either photo.
Both photos carry a faint dealer watermark reading roughly 'G.O MERCHANTS LTD'.
The photos show a whole container of stock; nothing shows which single engine, or how many, the advert is for.
The seller's text lists several different vehicle fitments (RX350, ES350, IS250, Camry) rather than one item.

identity.kind: foreign-used car engine (tokunbo engine), exact engine code unknown, from a container of mixed stock
read_from: photo 0 and photo 1 container of engines, no code readable

claims.evidence: No engine code or label readable in photo 0 or photo 1 to tie any unit to an RX350.
No engine code readable in either photo.
No engine code readable; an IS250 engine is a different engine from the RX350/ES350 one, so which is on offer matters.
No engine code readable; Camry came with four cylinder and V6 engines of different value.

risks.risk: The advert covers many different engines; which engine, and how many, is actually being sold is unknown, and engine code sets the price
risks.proof: Close photo of the specific engine offered showing the stamped engine code on the block, with a handwritten note bearing today's date
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced; no worst case without the engine code

risks.risk: Engine internals worn, knocking, or overheated (warped heads, low compression)
risks.proof: Video of the engine running on a test stand or a compression test reading on each cylinder
risks.if_unproven: as a non-running engine for rebuild or parts

risks.risk: Missing ancillaries: the units look like bare long blocks with parts possibly removed (intake, injectors, sensors, alternator, starter)
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides and top of the specific engine showing what is fitted

risks.risk: Cracked block or broken mounting ears from container handling
risks.proof: Close photos of the block sides, mounts and oil pan

risks.risk: Photos are dealer stock photos with a watermark and may not show the unit that would be delivered
risks.proof: Fresh photo of the chosen engine with the seller's handwritten note and date
risks.if_unproven: no money moves before the agent inspects the exact unit

proof_requests: Say which single engine is being sold and the quantity
Close photo of the stamped engine code on that engine's block, with a handwritten note bearing today's date
Photos of all sides of that engine showing fitted parts
Video of the engine running or a compression test result
response.reason: The photos show a container of mixed used engines and the advert lists engines for several different vehicles, so neither the engine code nor the quantity that sets the price can be read. Even a worst case price needs to know which engine is on offer.
